title: Redwood Inference for Healthcare & PHI-Adjacent Workloads (Draft One-Pager)
content:
Redwood Inference for Healthcare & PHI-Adjacent Workloads (DRAFT)
Customer-facing one-pager | Version: v0.7 | Last updated: 2025-05-18

Who this is for
Healthcare organizations and healthcare-adjacent software teams building LLM features where:
- Data may include PHI or be PHI-adjacent (e.g., clinical notes, encounter summaries, call transcripts, billing/coding artifacts)
- Security review and auditability are non-negotiable
- Deployment constraints include VPC isolation, on-prem requirements, strict retention controls, and enterprise identity integration

What Redwood Inference provides
Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For healthcare workloads, our focus is predictable performance (latency + throughput), deployment flexibility, and operational controls needed to support compliance programs.

Key capabilities for regulated healthcare environments
1) Private deployment options that match your environment
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved capacity with isolation and predictable throughput
- Redwood Private: deploy in your VPC (and on-prem options for restricted environments)
- Same API + operational tooling across environments to reduce integration and migration risk

2) Security controls and auditability designed for enterprise reviews
- Encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest (platform-managed or customer-managed keys depending on deployment)
- KMS/HSM integration patterns available for Private deployments (customer-managed key control)
- Role-based access control (RBAC) + enterprise identity options (SSO/SAML; SCIM where applicable)
- Audit logs to support operational traceability (who did what, when; administrative and access events)
- Evidence pack available under NDA for security review (SOC 2 process, diagrams, example log fields, and policy statements)

3) Operational controls for retention, residency, and access boundaries
- Configurable retention/residency patterns by deployment (e.g., keep inference traffic and logs in-region; isolate workloads per environment)
- Clear data boundary options (what is processed, what is stored, what is logged) aligned to your policies
- Built-in observability: token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-route/model dashboards, error analysis

4) Production economics without sacrificing reliability
- High-throughput serving runtime with batching/caching and smart routing for consistent SLOs
- Rollouts: canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies to maintain uptime
- Optimize toolkit: recommendations on batching/caching/quantization profiles for unit cost reduction

Common healthcare use cases (examples)
Member/patient support assistants
- Summarize conversations, suggest responses, route to the right department
- Guardrails: data minimization, strict logging controls, and least-privilege access

Clinical summarization (clinician-in-the-loop)
- Draft visit summaries or chart notes with sources and structured formats
- Guardrails: human review required; clear provenance; restrict outputs to templates

Coding & billing assistance
- Suggest ICD-10/CPT candidates, extract entities from structured/unstructured notes
- Guardrails: maintain audit trail; keep models and prompts versioned for change control

Quality & safety note: Redwood provides inference infrastructure. Customers are responsible for configuring prompts/workflows, implementing human oversight where required, and validating outputs for clinical or billing decisions.

Reference deployment patterns
Pattern A: VPC / private cloud deployment (recommended for PHI)
- Redwood Private control plane deployed into customer VPC
- Customer-managed networking (private subnets, security groups, egress controls)
- Optional customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption
- Centralized log export to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk/Sentinel) via supported export mechanisms

Pattern B: On-prem / restricted environment
- Redwood Private on-prem package for environments with strict network boundaries
- Local logging + export into customer systems
- Controlled upgrades and version pinning for change management

Pattern C: Dedicated capacity with isolation
- Reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput
- Strong fit when you need isolation + performance but don’t require full private control plane

What to expect in a short pilot (2–4 weeks)
Goal: Validate security fit + performance + operational readiness with a real workflow.
- Week 0 (prep): security questionnaire intake, architecture review, confirm data boundaries and retention expectations
- Week 1: connectivity + auth setup (SSO optional), baseline benchmark, logging/monitoring validation
- Week 2: workload evaluation on agreed dataset (de-identified/synthetic recommended when feasible), measure latency/cost/quality
- Closeout: results readout, recommended rollout plan, and procurement path (Dedicated vs Private)

Example success criteria (to tailor)
- Latency/throughput: meet agreed SLO targets for your workload profile
- Security: evidence pack review completed; audit logging and access controls validated
- Operations: monitoring dashboards and alerting integrated; log export path confirmed
- Commercial: clear packaging decision (Dedicated vs Private) and implementation timeline

What we can share during security review
Under NDA, we can provide an evidence index and selected artifacts (as applicable), including:
- SOC 2 report process and scope details
- Security architecture diagrams
- Example audit log field documentation
- Policy statements (incident response, access controls, retention)

CTA
Schedule a 30-minute security + architecture working session:
- We’ll map your workload to the right deployment pattern (VPC, on-prem, or dedicated)
- We’ll confirm the audit/retention/residency requirements upfront
- We’ll propose a pilot plan with clear owners and success criteria

Important notes on healthcare compliance language (draft-safe)
- Redwood does not provide legal advice. Your compliance team should determine how the platform fits your HIPAA/HITRUST policies.
- We avoid “HIPAA-certified” or “HIPAA compliant” claims. We position as: “supports HIPAA-aligned deployments and controls” (subject to your configuration and agreements).

OPEN QUESTIONS (Legal/Compliance review needed before final)
1) BAA posture:
- Can Redwood sign a BAA for Private and/or Dedicated? If yes, under what support tier and what minimum commercial terms?
- Any exclusions (e.g., Hosted API only with de-identified data)?

2) Marketing claim boundaries:
- Approved phrasing for: “PHI workloads,” “HIPAA-ready,” “HIPAA-aligned,” “supports HIPAA requirements.”
- Are we comfortable saying “PHI-adjacent” vs “PHI” in externally published assets?

3) Audit logging specifics:
- Which audit log categories/fields are approved to name externally (e.g., admin events, access events, policy changes)?
- Can we show a redacted sample audit log payload in this one-pager or only in the evidence pack?

4) Retention/residency:
- What retention controls are contractually supported today (logs, prompts, outputs) across Dedicated vs Private?
- Do we have approved language for regional residency commitments (US-only, EU-only) and exceptions?

5) Subprocessors + hosting details:
- Which deployment modes require disclosing cloud providers/subprocessors and what is the approved reference language?

6) Clinical safety disclaimers:
- Do we need stronger language about “not for clinical decision-making without qualified review” for certain use cases?
